title: Land surface temperature in Riyadh, summer 2026, by land cover and district

service.name: Land Surface Temperature and Urban Heat Islands

data: Landsat 9 Collection 2 Level-2, scene LC09_L2SP_166043_20260724_02_T1 (path 166 row 43, 24 July 2026, cloud 0%): surface temperature ST_B10, its uncertainty ST_QA, red and near-infrared surface reflectance and the QA_PIXEL layer, read as windows through the Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC API (collection landsat-c2-l2) with anonymous signing and no account.
method: Picked a cloud-free summer scene on path 166, which covers west and central Riyadh; path 165 cuts off the west.
Converted ST_B10 to temperature: value × 0.00341802 + 149.0 kelvin, minus 273.15, and masked pixels that QA_PIXEL flags as cloud, shadow or fill.
Districts: 130 of the 137 OpenStreetMap districts, after leaving out five eastern ones that fall partly outside the scene and two smaller than 18 ha (200 pixels).

Classes from OpenStreetMap: parks (leisure=park, 30 m in from the edge), green park pixels among them (NDVI ≥ 0.3 from the same scene), major roads (15 m either side of motorway, trunk and primary centrelines), residential, commercial and retail land use at least 60 m from those roads, and bare land (natural=sand, bare_rock, scree or desert).
limits: Surface temperature is not air temperature, and one overpass at about 10:20 am represents neither the whole day nor the whole summer. The thermal band is 100 m resampled to 30 m, so a road pixel mixes the road with its surroundings, and small parks and districts (Salam is 35 ha) take on their neighbours' values. Classes come from OpenStreetMap, whose completeness is not guaranteed: a mapped park may be vacant land and residential land use includes unbuilt plots.
